topClips.title: Top Clips
topClips.subtitle: A few bite-size moments from the talks — each clip plays for 10–20 seconds.

clips.videoTitle: Samuel M. Smith – Utah SEDI Public Identity Utility as bootstrap for AI Agent Surveillance Protection with KERI
clips.speaker: Samuel M. Smith
clips.quote: Does that feel like a world you'd like to live in? But you understand that that is the world we're in right now.

clips.videoTitle: Samuel M. Smith – Utah SEDI Public Identity Utility as bootstrap for AI Agent Surveillance Protection with KERI
clips.speaker: Samuel M. Smith
clips.quote: Continuous identity means I determine who you are by continuously surveilling everything that you do.

clips.videoTitle: Samuel M. Smith – Utah SEDI Public Identity Utility as bootstrap for AI Agent Surveillance Protection with KERI
clips.speaker: Samuel M. Smith
clips.quote: That just means you've created an arms race of surveillance.

clips.videoTitle: Samuel M. Smith – Utah SEDI Public Identity Utility as bootstrap for AI Agent Surveillance Protection with KERI
clips.speaker: Samuel M. Smith
clips.quote: The answer isn't continuous surveillance. It is just key management. If we do key management well, AI cyber can't attack us, can't attack you, can't attack anybody.

clips.videoTitle: Samuel M. Smith: The state and the future of the KERI Suite
clips.speaker: Samuel M. Smith
clips.quote: I call it the era of the ledger wars. Everybody decided that digital identity based on blockchain was the coolest thing.

clips.videoTitle: Samuel M. Smith & Ryan Hansen – Progress report: The 5W’s of KERI: Witnesses, Watchers, Wallet, Web, and Wizard PLUS Bulk issuances and anchoring in Merkle Trees
clips.speaker: Samuel M. Smith & Ryan Hansen
clips.quote: Without anchoring, you've missed most of the security properties of what KERI provides.

clips.videoTitle: Ryan Hansen & Samuel M. Smith –  Open infrastructure for KERI-based digital identity
clips.speaker: Ryan Hansen & Samuel M. Smith
clips.quote: If you have vendor lock-in, it's not open infrastructure. Open standards and open source aren't enough if users still can't leave.
